svg.title: Resolve Rights, Claims, Privacy, and Distribution before Release
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-publication-statutory-risk-checks; chart type: decision_tree; title: Resolve Rights, Claims, Privacy, and Distribution before Release; subtitle: Each affirmative answer advances; each negative answer triggers repair.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four sequential yes-or-no checks. A failed check sends the affected page, tracking feature, or outreach campaign to the named corrective action before reassessment. Statutory duties depend on the activity and applicable jurisdiction; search platform policies are separate contractual and distribution risks.; caption: Record evidence, the responsible owner, and the corrective action. Do not treat an automated SEO score as proof of copyright permission, truthful advertising, or lawful data handling.; stages: label: Rights established?; value: Yes: advance; no: replace or document permission; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Editor checks text, images, datasets, and contributor agreements against 17 U.S.C. 106, 107, and 204. Fair use requires specific analysis; attribution alone does not grant reproduction rights.; label: Commercial claims supportable?; value: Yes: advance; no: correct claims and disclosures; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Commercial lead checks evidence under 15 U.S.C. 45 and material connections under 16 CFR 255.5. Place clear disclosures with endorsements; do not bury paid relationships in a distant policy page.; label: Data handling scoped?; value: Yes: advance; no: disable affected collection; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Technical lead maps identifiers, recipients, retention, and applicable rights. Assess Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100, 1798.120, and 1798.140 applicability; assess COPPA under 15 U.S.C. 6502 and 16 CFR 312 for child-directed services or relevant actual knowledge.; label: Distribution method acceptable?; value: Yes: release; no: revise outreach or templates; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Operator checks commercial email against 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate headers and functioning opt-out. Separately inspect Google spam policies for scaled content abuse, link spam, and site reputation abuse.
